question: What is the function of the clause 'because the funds were insufficient' in: 'The project was canceled because the funds were insufficient.'?

question: What is the function of the clause 'that the budget was approved' in: 'The fact that the budget was approved pleased the team.'?

question: What is the function of the clause 'whether the policy should be revised' in: 'The question is whether the policy should be revised.'?

question: What is the function of the clause 'whose report was outstanding' in: 'The employee whose report was outstanding received recognition.'?

question: What is the function of the clause 'after the investigation is completed' in: 'The findings will be released after the investigation is completed.'?

question: Identify the noun clause and its function: 'I don't understand why the application was rejected.'

question: Identify the noun clause and its function: 'Whether he will accept the position remains uncertain.'

question: What type of dependent clause is 'that the deadline was extended' in: 'She confirmed that the deadline was extended.'?

question: What is the function of 'where the documents are stored' in: 'No one knows where the documents are stored.'?

question: What type of clause is 'provided that the requirements are met' in: 'The application will be processed provided that the requirements are met.'?

question: What is the function of 'whoever submits first' in: 'Whoever submits first will be prioritized.'?

question: What type of clause is 'where new employees are assigned' in: 'The office where new employees are assigned is on the second floor.'?

question: What is the function of 'how the error occurred' in: 'The investigation revealed how the error occurred.'?

question: What type of clause is 'so that employees can access the system remotely' in: 'The IT department upgraded the network so that employees can access the system remotely.'?

question: Identify the adjective clause: 'The regulation that was implemented last year has reduced violations significantly.'

question: Identify the adverb clause: 'The employees remained calm even though the situation was critical.'

question: Identify the noun clause: 'The supervisor asked whether the report had been submitted.'

question: Identify the independent clause: 'Although the training was optional, most employees attended because they wanted to improve their skills.'

they wanted to improve their skills

question: Identify the adjective clause: 'The candidate whom the panel recommended has accepted the position.'

question: Identify the adverb clause: 'Before the fiscal year ends, all departments must submit their budget proposals.'

question: Identify the noun clause: 'That the project was completed on time impressed the stakeholders.'
choices: That the project was completed on time
the project was completed on time

question: Identify the dependent clause: 'The manager will approve the request as soon as the documents are verified.'

as soon as the documents are verified

question: Identify the adjective clause: 'The office where the incident occurred has been temporarily closed.'

question: Identify the adverb clause: 'Unless the committee approves the amendment, the original policy will remain in effect.'
choices: the original policy will remain in effect

question: Identify the noun clause: 'The director explained how the new system would improve efficiency.'
choices: how the new system would improve efficiency
the new system would improve efficiency

explanation: 'How the new system would improve efficiency' is a noun clause functioning as the direct object of 'explained.'

question: Identify the adjective clause: 'The employees whose evaluations were outstanding received bonuses.'
explanation: 'Whose evaluations were outstanding' modifies 'employees' (tells which employees).

question: Identify the adverb clause: 'She completed the project ahead of schedule so that she could take her leave.'
choices: She completed the project ahead of schedule
so that she could take her leave

question: Identify the independent clause: 'While the audit was being conducted, the department continued its operations, and the staff cooperated fully.'

Both 'the department continued its operations' and 'the staff cooperated fully'

question: Identify the noun clause: 'No one is certain when the results will be released.'
choices: when the results will be released

question: Identify the adjective clause: 'The day when the new policy takes effect is approaching.'

question: Identify the adverb clause: 'The team worked overtime whereas the other department left on time.'

the other department left on time

question: Identify the dependent clause: 'The policy requires that all new hires complete orientation within their first week.'

question: Identify the adjective clause: 'The memorandum, which was circulated yesterday, outlines the new procedures.'

question: Identify the adverb clause: 'As long as the employee maintains satisfactory performance, the contract will be renewed.'

explanation: 'As long as the employee maintains satisfactory performance' is an adverb clause of condition.

question: Which sentence correctly combines these ideas? 'The report was thorough. It contained several factual errors.'

question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?

The policy that was revised, is now effective.

question: How many clauses are in this sentence? 'The manager who approved the budget confirmed that the project would start after the contracts were signed.'

question: Identify the sentence type: 'Although the budget was tight, the department completed the project, and the results exceeded expectations.'

question: What relationship does the dependent clause express? 'Although the candidate was qualified, she was not selected.'

question: In which sentence is 'that' a relative pronoun (introducing an adjective clause)?

question: Choose the correct sentence:

question: Identify the function of the clause 'that the funds which were allocated for the project that the committee approved would be released after the requirements are met' in: 'The director announced that the funds which were allocated for the project that the committee approved would be released after the requirements are met.'

question: In the sentence 'The regulation whose implementation was delayed because the agency that was responsible lacked the resources that were needed has finally taken effect,' how many dependent clauses are there?

explanation: The noun clause 'whoever the committee determines is most qualified' is the object of the preposition 'to.' Note: 'whoever' (not 'whomever') is correct because it is the subject of 'is most qualified.'

question: In the sentence 'Whether the policy that the committee which was formed last year proposed will be adopted depends on what the stakeholders decide,' identify the main independent clause structure.
explanation: The main clause structure is 'X depends on Y' where X is a noun clause subject and Y is a noun clause object of preposition. The independent clause skeleton is the entire sentence's main predicate structure.

question: How many clauses are in this sentence? 'The manager confirmed that the employee who was absent would return after the doctor cleared him.'
explanation: Four clauses: (1) 'The manager confirmed' (independent), (2) 'that the employee would return' (noun clause), (3) 'who was absent' (adjective clause), (4) 'after the doctor cleared him' (adverb clause).

question: In the sentence 'It is essential that whoever is appointed to the position that was vacated demonstrate that they can manage the team effectively,' identify all noun clauses.
explanation: Three noun clauses: (1) 'that whoever is appointed...demonstrate that they can manage the team effectively' (subject complement after 'is'), (2) 'whoever is appointed to the position that was vacated' (subject of 'demonstrate'), (3) 'that they can manage the team effectively' (direct object of 'demonstrate').

question: What type of clause is 'as if nothing had happened' in: 'The employee continued working as if nothing had happened.'?
explanation: 'As if nothing had happened' is an adverb clause of manner — it describes HOW the employee continued working.

question: In the sentence 'The question of whether the agency should implement what the consultant recommended before the fiscal year ends remains unresolved,' what is the function of 'what the consultant recommended'?
explanation: 'What the consultant recommended' is a noun clause functioning as the direct object of 'implement' (implement WHAT?).

question: Identify the sentence type: 'Although the budget was reduced, the department achieved its targets, and the director commended the staff who had worked overtime because the deadline was approaching.'
explanation: It has two independent clauses ('the department achieved its targets' and 'the director commended the staff') plus multiple dependent clauses ('Although the budget was reduced,' 'who had worked overtime,' 'because the deadline was approaching').

question: In 'The policy requires that all documents which are submitted after the deadline that the commission set be considered invalid unless the applicant provides evidence that the delay was unavoidable,' how many dependent clauses are there?
explanation: Five dependent clauses: (1) 'that all documents be considered invalid' (noun), (2) 'which are submitted after the deadline' (adjective), (3) 'that the commission set' (adjective), (4) 'unless the applicant provides evidence' (adverb), (5) 'that the delay was unavoidable' (noun/appositive).

question: What is the function of the clause 'where the incident occurred' in: 'The office where the incident occurred, which is located on the third floor, has been temporarily closed.'?
explanation: 'Where the incident occurred' modifies 'office' (tells WHICH office). Even though 'where' can introduce adverb clauses, here it functions as a relative adverb in an adjective clause.

question: In 'What concerns the board is not whether the project will succeed but whether the timeline that was proposed is realistic,' identify the main clause structure.
choices: 'What concerns the board IS not X but Y'
answer: 'What concerns the board IS not X but Y'
explanation: The main clause structure is 'Subject + linking verb + complement.' The subject is a noun clause, and the complement is a correlative structure with two noun clauses.

question: How many clauses does this sentence contain? 'The employee who was hired after the position that had been vacant since the previous occupant resigned was finally filled has already demonstrated exceptional competence.'
explanation: Five clauses: (1) 'The employee has demonstrated exceptional competence' (independent), (2) 'who was hired' (adjective), (3) 'after the position was finally filled' (adverb), (4) 'that had been vacant' (adjective), (5) 'since the previous occupant resigned' (adverb).

question: Is 'where she works' a noun clause or an adjective clause in: 'The building where she works is on Main Street.'?
explanation: 'Where she works' modifies the noun 'building' (tells which building). It is an adjective clause, not an adverb clause of place.

question: Is 'where she works' a noun clause or an adverb clause in: 'I don't know where she works.'?
explanation: 'Where she works' is the direct object of 'know' (know WHAT?). It functions as a noun, not as a modifier.

question: Is 'where she works' a noun clause or an adverb clause in: 'She is happy where she works.'?
explanation: 'Where she works' modifies the adjective 'happy' by telling where/in what situation she is happy. It functions as an adverb clause.

question: Is 'when the results are released' a noun clause or an adverb clause in: 'No one knows when the results are released.'?
explanation: 'When the results are released' is the direct object of 'knows' (knows WHAT?). It functions as a noun.

question: Is 'when the results are released' a noun clause or an adverb clause in: 'Everyone celebrates when the results are released.'?
explanation: 'When the results are released' modifies 'celebrates' by telling WHEN. It functions as an adverb clause.

question: What type of clause is 'that the committee approved' in: 'I know that the committee approved the proposal.'?
explanation: 'That the committee approved the proposal' is a noun clause — the direct object of 'know.' Here 'that' is a conjunction.

question: What type of clause is 'that the committee approved' in: 'The proposal that the committee approved was implemented.'?
explanation: 'That the committee approved' modifies 'proposal' (tells which proposal). Here 'that' is a relative pronoun.

question: In 'The fact that she resigned is what surprised everyone,' identify the types of both 'that' and 'what' clauses.
choices: 'that she resigned' is noun (appositive); 'what surprised everyone' is noun (complement)
'that she resigned' is adjective; 'what surprised everyone' is noun
answer: 'that she resigned' is noun (appositive); 'what surprised everyone' is noun (complement)
explanation: 'That she resigned' is a noun clause in apposition to 'fact.' 'What surprised everyone' is a noun clause functioning as the subject complement after 'is.'

question: What is the difference between 'since' in these sentences? (A) 'Since she arrived, things have improved.' (B) 'Since she is qualified, she should apply.'
explanation: In (A), 'since' means 'from the time that' (time). In (B), 'since' means 'because' (reason). Context determines the meaning.

question: What is the difference between 'while' in these sentences? (A) 'While she was working, he called.' (B) 'While she is diligent, he is lazy.'
explanation: In (A), 'while' means 'during the time that.' In (B), 'while' means 'whereas' (contrast).

question: In 'The report, which the director signed before the deadline that the commission had set, was distributed to all offices where new employees had been assigned,' identify all adjective clauses.
explanation: Three adjective clauses: (1) 'which the director signed before the deadline that the commission had set' (modifies 'report'), (2) 'that the commission had set' (modifies 'deadline'), (3) 'where new employees had been assigned' (modifies 'offices').

question: Is 'whoever applies' the subject or object in: 'The scholarship will be awarded to whoever applies first.'?
explanation: The entire noun clause 'whoever applies first' is the object of the preposition 'to.' Note: 'whoever' (not 'whomever') is correct because it is the subject within its own clause ('whoever applies').

question: In 'I will support whomever the committee selects,' why is 'whomever' correct instead of 'whoever'?
choices: It is the object of 'selects' within the clause
It is the subject of the noun clause
answer: It is the object of 'selects' within the clause
explanation: 'Whomever' is correct because within the noun clause, it is the object of 'selects' (the committee selects WHOM). The entire clause 'whomever the committee selects' is the object of 'support.'

question: What type of clause is 'as though she had not heard the announcement' in: 'She continued working as though she had not heard the announcement.'?
explanation: 'As though' introduces a clause describing the manner of the action — how she continued working.

question: In 'The question is not whether we should act but how we should act,' identify the clause types of both underlined portions.
choices: First is noun clause, second is adverb clause
explanation: Both 'whether we should act' and 'how we should act' are noun clauses functioning as subject complements in a correlative structure ('not X but Y').

question: What is the function of 'that he would resign if the investigation proved that the allegations were true' in: 'The official announced that he would resign if the investigation proved that the allegations were true.'?
explanation: The entire complex noun clause (containing embedded adverb and noun clauses) is the direct object of 'announced.'

question: Which sentence contains a clause error?
choices: The employee whom the director praised was promoted.
The policy which was revised takes effect Monday.
The officer whom filed the report is on leave.
The regulation that the committee approved is strict.
answer: The officer whom filed the report is on leave.
explanation: 'Whom' is incorrect here. The pronoun is the SUBJECT of 'filed' (he/she filed), so 'who' is required.

question: Which sentence contains a clause error?
choices: What the director said was surprising.
The reason is because the funds were insufficient.
Whether the policy changes depends on the committee.
answer: The reason is because the funds were insufficient.
explanation: 'The reason is because...' is redundant. Correct: 'The reason is that the funds were insufficient.'

question: Which sentence contains a misplaced adjective clause?
choices: The supervisor praised the employee who completed the project early.
The employee submitted the report to the director who was incomplete.
The officer who investigated the case filed a detailed report.
The policy that the committee approved takes effect Monday.
answer: The employee submitted the report to the director who was incomplete.
explanation: 'Who was incomplete' illogically modifies 'director.' The clause should modify 'report': 'The employee submitted the report, which was incomplete, to the director.'

question: Which sentence has incorrect punctuation for its clause structure?
choices: The employees who passed the exam will be promoted.
The director, who has served for twenty years, announced her retirement.
The policy, that was revised last year, is now effective.
Although the task was difficult, she completed it on time.
answer: The policy, that was revised last year, is now effective.
explanation: 'That' introduces restrictive clauses — no commas. Either remove commas (restrictive with 'that') or change to 'which' with commas (non-restrictive).

question: Which sentence contains a dangling or misattached clause?
choices: After reviewing the documents, the committee made its decision.
After reviewing the documents, a decision was made by the committee.
Because the budget was approved, the project commenced.
Although she was new, she performed excellently.
answer: After reviewing the documents, a decision was made by the committee.
explanation: The participial phrase 'After reviewing the documents' dangles — 'a decision' cannot review documents. The subject should be 'the committee.'

question: Which sentence incorrectly uses 'which' instead of 'that'?
choices: The building, which was constructed in 1990, needs renovation.
The regulation which requires all employees to attend is strict.
The memorandum, which was issued yesterday, outlines new procedures.
The award, which is given annually, recognizes excellence.
answer: The regulation which requires all employees to attend is strict.
explanation: This is a restrictive clause (identifies WHICH regulation), so 'that' should be used without commas: 'The regulation that requires all employees to attend is strict.'

question: Which sentence has a subject-verb agreement error involving a noun clause?
choices: What the employees want is better working conditions.
What the employees want are better working conditions.
Whether the changes are effective remains to be seen.
That the reports were late is unacceptable.
answer: What the employees want are better working conditions.
explanation: When a noun clause subject refers to a single concept, the verb should be singular: 'What the employees want IS better working conditions.' The subject is the clause itself (singular), not 'conditions.'

question: Which sentence incorrectly separates a noun clause from its verb with a comma?
choices: I believe that she is qualified.
What the committee decided, is final.
She confirmed that the deadline was extended.
Whether he attends is his decision.
answer: What the committee decided, is final.
explanation: No comma should separate a noun clause subject from its verb. Correct: 'What the committee decided is final.'

question: Which sentence contains a fragment disguised as a complex sentence?
choices: Although the report was submitted on time, it contained errors.
Because the meeting was canceled and the staff had already left the building.
Unless you submit the form, your application will not be processed.
After the audit was completed, the findings were presented.
answer: Because the meeting was canceled and the staff had already left the building.
explanation: This contains two dependent clauses joined by 'and' but no independent clause — it is a fragment despite its length.

question: Which sentence has an error in relative pronoun usage?
choices: The employee whose performance improved received a bonus.
The candidate who's application was accepted starts Monday.
The officer whom we interviewed was impressive.
The regulation that was implemented reduced violations.
answer: The candidate who's application was accepted starts Monday.
explanation: 'Who's' means 'who is' — it is a contraction, not a possessive. The correct form is 'whose' (possessive relative pronoun).

question: Which sentence incorrectly uses a subordinating conjunction?
choices: Although she was qualified, she was not hired.
Unless you apply, you will not be considered.
Because of she was late, the meeting started without her.
Since the policy changed, compliance has improved.
answer: Because of she was late, the meeting started without her.
explanation: 'Because of' is a preposition requiring a noun phrase, not a clause. Correct: 'Because she was late...' (conjunction + clause) or 'Because of her lateness...' (preposition + noun).

question: Which sentence has a clause structure error?
choices: The director confirmed that the project would proceed.
She asked that whether the training was mandatory.
The committee decided that the policy should be revised.
I believe that the deadline should be extended.
answer: She asked that whether the training was mandatory.
explanation: Using both 'that' and 'whether' is redundant. Correct: 'She asked whether the training was mandatory.'

question: Which sentence incorrectly uses 'whom'?
choices: The applicant whom we selected starts Monday.
To whom should I address the letter?
The officer whom is responsible should report immediately.
The candidate whom the panel recommended was hired.
answer: The officer whom is responsible should report immediately.
explanation: 'Whom' is incorrect because the pronoun is the SUBJECT of 'is responsible.' Correct: 'The officer who is responsible...'

question: Which sentence has a comma splice that involves a dependent clause?
choices: She was tired, so she left early.
Although she was tired, she continued working.
She was tired, although she continued working.
She was tired, she continued working although it was late.
answer: She was tired, she continued working although it was late.
explanation: The first two clauses ('She was tired' and 'she continued working') are independent clauses joined by only a comma — a comma splice. The 'although' clause only modifies the second independent clause.

question: Which sentence has an error in clause punctuation?
choices: The employees, who all passed the exam, were promoted.
The employees who passed the exam were promoted.
The employees who passed the exam, were promoted.
Although the task was difficult, she completed it.
answer: The employees who passed the exam, were promoted.
explanation: A comma should not separate the subject ('The employees who passed the exam') from its verb ('were promoted'). The restrictive clause is part of the subject.

question: In the sentence 'The memorandum states that all personnel whose contracts expire before the end of the fiscal year must submit renewal applications unless they have already been notified that their positions have been abolished,' which clause is the direct object of 'states'?
choices: 'that all personnel whose contracts expire...must submit renewal applications unless...'
'whose contracts expire before the end of the fiscal year'
answer: 'that all personnel whose contracts expire...must submit renewal applications unless...'
explanation: The entire complex noun clause beginning with 'that' is the direct object of 'states.' It contains multiple embedded dependent clauses within it.

question: Which analysis is correct for the sentence 'What the audit revealed was that the department had been operating without the authorization that the law requires'?
choices: Two noun clauses and one adjective clause
One noun clause and two adjective clauses
Two adjective clauses and one adverb clause
answer: Two noun clauses and one adjective clause
explanation: 'What the audit revealed' (noun clause/subject), 'that the department had been operating without the authorization' (noun clause/complement), 'that the law requires' (adjective clause modifying 'authorization').

question: In 'Provided that the applicant demonstrates that she possesses the qualifications that the position requires, the committee will recommend that she be appointed,' how many 'that' clauses are there and what are their types?
choices: Two noun clauses, one adjective clause
One adverb clause, two noun clauses, one adjective clause
Two adjective clauses, two noun clauses
answer: One adverb clause, two noun clauses, one adjective clause
explanation: 'Provided that the applicant demonstrates...' (adverb/condition), 'that she possesses the qualifications' (noun/object of 'demonstrates'), 'that the position requires' (adjective modifying 'qualifications'), 'that she be appointed' (noun/object of 'recommend').

question: Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive mood in a noun clause?
choices: The committee recommended that he is promoted.
The committee recommended that he be promoted.
The committee recommended that he was promoted.
The committee recommended that he will be promoted.
answer: The committee recommended that he be promoted.
explanation: After verbs of recommendation/demand (recommend, suggest, insist, require), the noun clause uses the subjunctive: base form of the verb ('be,' not 'is/was/will be').

question: Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive in a noun clause?
choices: It is essential that every employee attends the training.
It is essential that every employee attend the training.
It is essential that every employee will attend the training.
It is essential that every employee is attending the training.
answer: It is essential that every employee attend the training.
explanation: After 'it is essential/important/necessary that...,' the subjunctive (base form) is used: 'attend' (not 'attends').

question: In 'The director, whose tenure has been marked by reforms that have transformed the agency since she assumed office, announced that she would step down after the transition that the board had planned was completed,' identify the main clause.
choices: 'whose tenure has been marked by reforms'
'The director announced that she would step down'
answer: 'The director announced that she would step down'
explanation: The main independent clause skeleton is 'The director announced [noun clause].' Everything else is embedded dependent clauses.

question: Which sentence demonstrates correct parallel structure in noun clauses?
choices: The report shows that revenue increased and expenses have been reduced.
The report shows that revenue increased and that expenses decreased.
The report shows that revenue increased and decreasing expenses.
The report shows that revenue increased, expenses decreased.
answer: The report shows that revenue increased and that expenses decreased.
explanation: Parallel noun clauses should both begin with 'that' for clarity and grammatical parallelism.

question: In 'Whether the regulation that was proposed by the committee which oversees compliance will be adopted before the legislative session that begins next month ends depends on factors that no one can predict,' what is the subject of the main verb 'depends'?
explanation: The entire complex noun clause beginning with 'Whether' is the subject of 'depends.' It contains multiple embedded clauses.

question: Which sentence correctly handles a noun clause after a preposition?
choices: She is concerned about that the project might fail.
She is concerned about whether the project might fail.
She is concerned about the project might fail.
She is concerned that about the project might fail.
answer: She is concerned about whether the project might fail.
explanation: 'Whether' can follow a preposition. 'That' clauses generally cannot directly follow prepositions in standard English (use 'the fact that' instead).

question: Which analysis is correct for 'It remains to be seen whether what the new administration proposes will address the concerns that stakeholders have raised since the policy was first implemented'?
explanation: Four dependent clauses: (1) 'whether what...will address the concerns' (noun clause), (2) 'what the new administration proposes' (noun clause/subject within #1), (3) 'that stakeholders have raised' (adjective modifying 'concerns'), (4) 'since the policy was first implemented' (adverb of time).

question: Which sentence correctly uses an adverb clause of condition with the subjunctive?
choices: If I was the director, I would change the policy.
If I were the director, I would change the policy.
If I am the director, I would change the policy.
If I would be the director, I would change the policy.
answer: If I were the director, I would change the policy.
explanation: The subjunctive 'were' is used in hypothetical/contrary-to-fact conditions ('If I were...' not 'If I was...').

question: In 'The investigation determined that the official who had been entrusted with the funds that were allocated for the program that serves underprivileged communities had been misappropriating them since he assumed the position,' what does the adjective clause 'that serves underprivileged communities' modify?
explanation: The clause 'that serves underprivileged communities' immediately follows and modifies 'the program.'

question: Which sentence uses a reduced adjective clause correctly?
choices: The documents submitted yesterday contained errors.
The documents were submitted yesterday contained errors.
The documents submitting yesterday contained errors.
The documents submit yesterday contained errors.
answer: The documents submitted yesterday contained errors.
explanation: 'Submitted yesterday' is a reduced adjective clause (from 'that were submitted yesterday'). The past participle correctly modifies 'documents.'

question: Which sentence uses a reduced adverb clause correctly?
choices: While reviewing the documents, the committee found discrepancies.
While reviewing the documents, discrepancies were found.
While reviewed the documents, the committee found discrepancies.
While the reviewing documents, the committee found discrepancies.
answer: While reviewing the documents, the committee found discrepancies.
explanation: The reduced adverb clause 'While reviewing the documents' correctly shares its subject with the main clause ('the committee').

question: In 'Lest the committee forget that the deadline that was set by the regulation which governs procurement is non-negotiable, the director issued a reminder,' what type of clause is 'Lest the committee forget...'?
explanation: 'Lest' means 'for fear that' or 'so that...not.' It introduces an adverb clause of negative purpose.

question: Which sentence correctly embeds a noun clause within an adjective clause?
choices: The employee who believes that the policy is unfair filed a complaint.
The employee who believes the policy is unfair that filed a complaint.
The employee that who believes the policy is unfair filed a complaint.
The employee believes who that the policy is unfair filed a complaint.
answer: The employee who believes that the policy is unfair filed a complaint.
explanation: The adjective clause 'who believes that the policy is unfair' contains an embedded noun clause 'that the policy is unfair' (object of 'believes').

question: What is the error in: 'The reason why the project failed is because the team lacked resources.'?
explanation: 'The reason is because...' is redundant (reason already implies cause). Correct: 'The reason is that the team lacked resources.'

question: Which sentence correctly uses a cleft construction with a noun clause?
choices: It was the director who approved the budget.
It was that the director approved the budget.
What approved the budget was the director it.
The director it was who approved the budget.
answer: It was the director who approved the budget.
explanation: The cleft construction 'It was X who/that...' correctly emphasizes 'the director.' The adjective clause 'who approved the budget' modifies the focused element.

question: In 'Not until the committee certifies that the requirements have been met will the funds be released,' identify the clause type of 'that the requirements have been met.'
explanation: 'That the requirements have been met' is the direct object of 'certifies' (certifies WHAT?). The inverted word order doesn't change clause functions.

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'whether or not' in a noun clause?
choices: Whether or not she attends the meeting is her decision.
Whether or not, she attends the meeting is her decision.
She attends the meeting whether or not is her decision.
Whether she attends or not the meeting is her decision.
answer: Whether or not she attends the meeting is her decision.
explanation: 'Whether or not she attends the meeting' is a noun clause functioning as the subject. 'Whether or not' correctly precedes the subject of the embedded clause.

question: Which sentence best combines these ideas using appropriate clause structure? 'The policy was implemented. The committee had concerns. The concerns were about its feasibility.'
choices: The policy was implemented although the committee had concerns about its feasibility.
The policy was implemented, the committee had concerns about its feasibility.
Although the committee had concerns about its feasibility, the policy was implemented.
The policy was implemented and the committee had concerns about its feasibility.
answer: Although the committee had concerns about its feasibility, the policy was implemented.
explanation: 'Although' correctly shows concession (implemented despite concerns), and placing the dependent clause first emphasizes the contrast.

question: Which revision best corrects this sentence? 'The employee submitted the report. Who was assigned to the project.'
choices: The employee submitted the report, who was assigned to the project.
The employee who was assigned to the project submitted the report.
The employee submitted the report who was assigned to the project.
Who was assigned to the project, the employee submitted the report.
answer: The employee who was assigned to the project submitted the report.
explanation: The adjective clause 'who was assigned to the project' must immediately follow the noun it modifies ('employee').

question: Which sentence correctly transforms the direct question into an embedded noun clause? Direct: 'When will the results be released?'
choices: I want to know when will the results be released.
I want to know when the results will be released.
I want to know when are the results released.
I want to know when the results are will be released.
answer: I want to know when the results will be released.
explanation: In embedded (indirect) questions, use statement word order (subject before verb): 'when the results will be released' (not 'when will the results').

question: Which sentence correctly transforms the direct question into an embedded noun clause? Direct: 'Has the committee made a decision?'
choices: I wonder has the committee made a decision.
I wonder whether the committee has made a decision.
I wonder that the committee has made a decision.
I wonder if has the committee made a decision.
answer: I wonder whether the committee has made a decision.
explanation: Yes/no questions become 'whether/if' clauses with statement word order in indirect speech.

question: Which sentence correctly uses a noun clause as the subject with appropriate verb agreement?
choices: That the reports were submitted late are unacceptable.
That the reports were submitted late is unacceptable.
That the reports were submitted late were unacceptable.
That the reports were submitted late have been unacceptable.
answer: That the reports were submitted late is unacceptable.
explanation: A noun clause subject takes a singular verb ('is'), regardless of plural nouns within the clause.

question: Which sentence correctly reduces 'The employees who were hired last month' to a participial phrase?
choices: The employees hiring last month attended the orientation.
The employees hired last month attended the orientation.
The employees who hiring last month attended the orientation.
The employees were hired last month attended the orientation.
answer: The employees hired last month attended the orientation.
explanation: 'Hired last month' is a reduced adjective clause (past participle phrase) from 'who were hired last month.'

question: Which sentence correctly uses a noun clause after 'the fact that' to follow a preposition?
choices: She was upset about that the project was canceled.
She was upset about the fact that the project was canceled.
She was upset about the project was canceled.
She was upset the fact about that the project was canceled.
answer: She was upset about the fact that the project was canceled.
explanation: 'That' clauses cannot directly follow prepositions. Use 'the fact that' as a bridge: 'about the fact that...'

question: In 'Had the committee known that the contractor whom they had selected lacked the certification that the regulation requires, they would not have awarded the contract,' identify the conditional clause.
explanation: 'Had the committee known' is an inverted conditional clause (formal equivalent of 'If the committee had known'). It is an adverb clause of condition.

question: Which sentence correctly uses parallel noun clauses?
choices: The report shows that revenue increased, expenses decreased, and the workforce expanded.
The report shows that revenue increased, that expenses decreased, and that the workforce expanded.
The report shows that revenue increased, expenses have decreased, and expanding the workforce.
The report shows revenue increased, that expenses decreased, and that the workforce expanded.
answer: The report shows that revenue increased, that expenses decreased, and that the workforce expanded.
explanation: For clarity and parallelism, each noun clause in a series should begin with 'that.'

question: Which sentence correctly handles the ambiguity of 'since'?
choices: Since the director left, the department has improved. (time)
Since the director is qualified, she should be promoted. (reason)
Both A and B are correct uses of 'since'
Neither A nor B is correct
answer: Both A and B are correct uses of 'since'
explanation: 'Since' can mean 'from the time that' (time) or 'because' (reason). Both uses are grammatically correct; context determines meaning.

question: Which sentence correctly uses a concessive clause with inversion?
choices: Though she is experienced, she was not hired.
Experienced though she is, she was not hired.
Though experienced she is, she was not hired.
She is experienced though, she was not hired.
answer: Experienced though she is, she was not hired.
explanation: 'Adjective + though + subject + verb' is a formal inverted concessive structure. It emphasizes the concession.

question: In 'So complex was the regulation that even the lawyers who specialize in administrative law found that they could not determine what the provision that was added at the last minute actually required,' identify the result clause.
choices: 'that even the lawyers who specialize in administrative law found that they could not determine what...'
answer: 'that even the lawyers who specialize in administrative law found that they could not determine what...'
explanation: In the 'so...that' construction, the 'that' clause expresses the result of the extreme degree ('so complex').

question: Which sentence correctly uses a noun clause in apposition?
choices: The idea, that we should postpone the project, was rejected.
The idea that we should postpone the project was rejected.
The idea we should postpone the project that was rejected.
That we should postpone the project the idea was rejected.
answer: The idea that we should postpone the project was rejected.
explanation: A noun clause in apposition to 'idea' uses 'that' without commas (it defines what the idea IS). This is different from a non-restrictive adjective clause.

question: Which analysis is correct for 'It is not clear whether the amendment that the opposition proposed, which would have required that all agencies submit quarterly reports, will be included in the final version that the president signs.'?
explanation: Five: (1) 'whether the amendment will be included' (noun clause), (2) 'that the opposition proposed' (adjective), (3) 'which would have required that all agencies submit quarterly reports' (adjective, non-restrictive), (4) 'that all agencies submit quarterly reports' (noun, object of 'required'), (5) 'that the president signs' (adjective modifying 'version').

question: Which sentence demonstrates correct use of a free relative clause (nominal relative clause)?
choices: Whatever the committee decides will be final.
Whatever the committee decides, will be final.
The committee decides whatever will be final.
Will be final whatever the committee decides.
answer: Whatever the committee decides will be final.
explanation: 'Whatever the committee decides' is a free relative clause (noun clause without an antecedent) functioning as the subject. No comma separates it from the verb.

question: In 'The official denied that he had known that the funds which had been earmarked for the project that the legislature approved were being diverted to accounts that he controlled,' how many clauses beginning with 'that' are there?
explanation: Four 'that' clauses: (1) 'that he had known...' (noun/object of 'denied'), (2) 'that the funds were being diverted' (noun/object of 'known'), (3) 'that the legislature approved' (adjective modifying 'project'), (4) 'that he controlled' (adjective modifying 'accounts'). Plus 'which had been earmarked' uses 'which.'

question: Which sentence correctly uses an adverb clause with 'no sooner...than'?
choices: No sooner had she arrived when the meeting started.
No sooner had she arrived than the meeting started.
No sooner she had arrived than the meeting started.
No sooner had she arrived that the meeting started.
answer: No sooner had she arrived than the meeting started.
explanation: 'No sooner...than' is the correct correlative structure with inverted word order ('had she arrived').

question: Which sentence correctly handles a noun clause after 'insist'?
choices: She insists that he attends the meeting.
She insists that he attend the meeting.
She insists that he will attend the meeting.
She insists that he is attending the meeting.
answer: She insists that he attend the meeting.
explanation: After 'insist' (a mandative verb), the noun clause uses the subjunctive: base form 'attend' (not 'attends').

question: In 'Not only did the investigation reveal that the official had been negligent, but it also showed that the system which was supposed to prevent such failures had been compromised by those who were tasked with maintaining it,' how many dependent clauses are there?
explanation: Four dependent clauses: (1) 'that the official had been negligent' (noun clause), (2) 'that the system...had been compromised by those who were tasked with maintaining it' (noun clause), (3) 'which was supposed to prevent such failures' (adjective clause), (4) 'who were tasked with maintaining it' (adjective clause).

question: Which sentence correctly uses a conditional clause with mixed time reference?
choices: If she studied harder yesterday, she will pass tomorrow.
If she had studied harder yesterday, she would pass tomorrow.
If she would have studied harder yesterday, she will pass tomorrow.
If she studies harder yesterday, she would pass tomorrow.
answer: If she had studied harder yesterday, she would pass tomorrow.
explanation: Mixed conditional: past condition ('had studied' — past perfect for unreal past) + present/future result ('would pass' — would + base form).

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'whether' vs 'if' in a noun clause?
choices: Whether or not she attends is her decision.
If or not she attends is her decision.
Whether she attends is her decision, or not.
If she attends or not is her decision.
answer: Whether or not she attends is her decision.
explanation: 'Whether' (not 'if') is used when the noun clause is the subject. 'If' cannot introduce subject noun clauses.

question: In 'The committee recommended that the regulation be revised so that it would address the concerns that stakeholders had raised before the policy was implemented,' what is the function of 'that the regulation be revised'?
explanation: 'That the regulation be revised' is a noun clause (direct object of 'recommended'). Note the subjunctive 'be revised.'

question: Which sentence correctly uses a cleft sentence to emphasize time?
choices: It was yesterday when the director announced the changes.
It was yesterday that the director announced the changes.
Yesterday it was that the director announced the changes.
It was that yesterday the director announced the changes.
answer: It was yesterday that the director announced the changes.
explanation: In cleft sentences emphasizing adverbs of time, 'that' (not 'when') is used: 'It was [focused element] that [rest of sentence].'

question: Which sentence correctly uses a pseudo-cleft (wh-cleft) construction?
choices: What the department needs is additional funding.
What the department needs are additional funding.
The department needs is what additional funding.
Additional funding is what the department needs it.
answer: What the department needs is additional funding.
explanation: The wh-cleft 'What X is Y' uses a noun clause as subject. The linking verb 'is' agrees with the clause (singular).

question: In 'Inasmuch as the evidence that was presented during the hearing which lasted three days demonstrated that the accused had violated the regulation that prohibits conflicts of interest, the committee had no choice but to recommend dismissal,' identify the main clause.
choices: 'the committee had no choice but to recommend dismissal'
answer: 'the committee had no choice but to recommend dismissal'
explanation: The main independent clause is 'the committee had no choice but to recommend dismissal.' Everything before the comma is a complex adverb clause of reason ('Inasmuch as...').

question: Which sentence correctly uses 'however' as a free relative (not a conjunctive adverb)?
choices: However difficult the task may be, she will complete it.
The task is difficult; however, she will complete it.
However, the task is difficult, she will complete it.
She will complete it however the task is difficult.
answer: However difficult the task may be, she will complete it.
explanation: 'However difficult the task may be' is a concessive free relative clause (= 'no matter how difficult'). It functions as an adverb clause.

question: Which analysis is correct for the sentence 'The fact that what the whistleblower alleged turned out to be true vindicated those who had believed that the system was corrupt'?
explanation: Four: (1) 'that what the whistleblower alleged turned out to be true' (noun clause in apposition to 'fact'), (2) 'what the whistleblower alleged' (noun clause/subject within #1), (3) 'who had believed that the system was corrupt' (adjective clause), (4) 'that the system was corrupt' (noun clause/object of 'believed').

question: Which sentence correctly uses a conditional clause with 'were to'?
choices: If the director were to resign, the department would be restructured.
If the director was to resign, the department would be restructured.
If the director would resign, the department were to be restructured.
Were the director to resign, the department will be restructured.
answer: If the director were to resign, the department would be restructured.
explanation: 'Were to + infinitive' expresses a hypothetical future condition. It is more formal than simple past subjunctive.

question: In 'So thoroughly had the auditors examined the records that they discovered discrepancies that no one who had previously reviewed the documents that were filed before the new system was implemented had noticed,' identify the result clause.
choices: 'So thoroughly had the auditors examined the records'
'that they discovered discrepancies that no one...had noticed'
answer: 'that they discovered discrepancies that no one...had noticed'
explanation: In the 'so...that' construction, the entire 'that' clause (including its embedded clauses) expresses the result.
